D021-D017_h001.question:
I guess this all really started getting noticeable around six months ago. I’ve always watched my weight because in retail, especially managing the women’s department, you’re kind of on display all day. But it’s gotten more rigid. Now I won’t touch bread, rice, pasta, or anything that feels “heavy.” I pick at salads, grilled chicken, coffee. If something looks oily, I just can’t make myself eat it.  

Everyone keeps telling me I’m “too thin,” but when I look in the mirror, I still see places that look bulky or out of proportion. My clothes hang differently, but I don’t trust what I see. I feel like if I let up even a little, I’ll blow up overnight. The idea of gaining weight makes me really anxious, almost panicky, so I keep trying to drop a bit more, tightening what I eat.  

I find myself checking my reflection in the store mirrors way more than I used to, adjusting my jacket, sucking in my stomach, comparing myself to customers. It’s on my mind most of the day, and it’s getting exhausting, but I can’t shake the feeling that my body still isn’t right.
D021-D017_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D021-D017_h001.answer: A & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h002.question:
I guess this all really started maybe a few months ago. I don’t have an exact date, but it’s been long enough that my wife keeps bringing it up. I’ve always tried to stay in shape for the job, but lately it’s like I can’t turn it off.  

I’ve cut way back on how much I’m eating. I’ll push my food around, take a couple bites, say I’m not that hungry. At work I tell the guys I already ate, so I just sip coffee. Even when I feel lightheaded on long shifts, I still tell myself I need to “tighten up” more.  

I know I’m already on the slimmer side, my belt’s down a couple notches, but every time I look in the mirror I just see parts of me that look wrong or “too much.” It’s not just the number on the scale, it’s how I look in the uniform, in regular clothes. I weigh myself multiple times a day, and if it’s even half a pound up, I get this rush of panic and start planning how to eat even less.  

My wife says I’m disappearing; I just feel like I’m still not where I should be.
D021-D017_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D021-D017_h002.answer: A & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D021-D017_h003.question:

I find myself staring at my body a lot, picking apart little things that look “off” to me, but it’s hard to explain exactly what. I just feel wrong in my own skin. Even when other people say I look fine, I can’t shake the feeling something about how I look isn’t right.

I guess the main thing is that food has started to feel…technical to me, like a system I need to control. Over the past few months I’ve been cutting out certain stuff—bread, rice, anything fried, most sauces—because I don’t like the idea of “unnecessary” calories. I tell people it’s just “clean eating,” but it’s gotten pretty rigid. If a team lunch is pizza or something, I’ll just say I already ate or I’m not hungry.

I check my weight a lot. The scale’s in my bathroom and I’ll step on it multiple times a day, sometimes before and after I eat. If the number goes up even a little, I feel this rush of panic, like I’ve messed up a build and everything’s going to spiral. Then I’ll tighten up what I eat even more.

My parents and a couple friends have said I’m going too far, but I honestly think they’re overreacting. From my point of view I’m just trying not to let myself get out of control.
